faq.a: An IPO is when a private company offers its shares to the public for the first time, allowing anyone to buy a part of the company.

faq.q: How do I apply for an IPO?
faq.a: You can apply for an IPO through your stockbroker using the ASBA (Applications Supported by Blocked Amount) facility, which blocks the application amount in your bank account until shares are allotted.

faq.q: What is a lot size in an IPO?
faq.a: A lot size is the minimum number of shares you must apply for in an IPO. You cannot bid for fewer shares than the specified lot size.

faq.q: What is the difference between a Mainboard IPO and an SME IPO?
faq.a: Mainboard IPOs are for larger companies and list on the main exchanges (NSE and BSE), while SME IPOs are for Small and Medium Enterprises and list on dedicated SME platforms like NSE Emerge or BSE SME, with different regulations and market capitalisation requirements.
The issue price, also known as the IPO price, is the fixed price at which the company offers its shares to the public during the IPO process.
